title: Flaky Moroccan Flatbreads with Date Syrup
summary: Thin, flaky Moroccan-style flatbreads served warm with a simple honeyless date syrup. They’re crisp at the edges, soft inside, and perfect for a light breakfast with tea.
steps: Make the date syrup first. Put the dates, water, lemon juice, cinnamon, and a pinch of salt into a small saucepan.
Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, then cook for 8 to 10 minutes until the dates are very soft and the liquid looks syrupy.
Blend until smooth, or mash very well for a rustic syrup, then set aside to cool slightly.
For the flatbread dough, mix the flour, salt, and baking powder in a large bowl.
Add the warm water and 15 ml of the olive oil, then stir until a shaggy dough forms.
Knead for 5 to 7 minutes until smooth and elastic. Cover and rest for 15 minutes.
Divide the dough into 4 balls. Lightly oil your work surface and stretch or press each ball into a very thin round.
Brush a little olive oil over the surface, fold or pleat the dough into a square package, then gently flatten again to create flaky layers.
Heat a dry frying pan over medium heat. Cook each flatbread for 2 to 3 minutes per side, pressing lightly, until golden brown with crisp, blistered spots.
Serve the flatbreads warm with the date syrup for dipping or drizzling. Pour tea alongside if desired.
